author: niklas_anzinger
description:
Montana passed a law called SB535. It builds on right-to-try (pre-approval access with informed consent, Phase 1 safety data etc.) but goes much further, fixing problems with those laws.

Alex Tabarrok called it "the most important regulatory innovation in drug approval in my lifetime" (https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2026/06/mo...). Was posted here but died in /new (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48559525). The mods suggested this post.

I contributed ideas to the law and am now implementing it through my company. I invested in biotech for years and watched companies struggle. I built the biotech ecosystem in Prospera as an alternative, concluded it was too early, and now think Montana is the best place to prove this.

Why this exists: W
title: Tell HN: An inside view of Montana's new biotech law
